question.text: Interest rate risk for bonds means:

answer.text: Bond prices rise when interest rates rise
Bond prices fall when interest rates rise, and vice versa — an inverse relationship
Bond coupon rates automatically change with market rates
Interest rate changes have no effect on bond prices

explanation.text: The Logic: Interest rate risk is the inverse relationship between bond prices and market interest rates: when interest rates rise, existing fixed-rate bond prices fall, and when interest rates fall, bond prices rise. Duration (and modified duration) measures the sensitivity of a bond's price to a change in interest rates. The Trap: Option A reverses the relationship. Option C describes floating-rate bonds, whose coupons reset to market rates, not fixed-rate bonds whose coupons do not change. Option D contradicts the inverse price-rate relationship. Note: Distributor's Pro-Tip and cross-exam coaching removed; explanation rewritten with the source's inverse rate-price relationship and duration sensitivity.
